Each FAIL withdrew a named prior independent approval taken at base 553966eaa41173d16111f55ca53216c6bf88b1f1 on bytes that never moved. Consolidated onto one lane because the three share one defect class and one remedy.

theBytesDidNotMoveBeforeThisLaneTouchedT.why: vf02, vf03 and vf04 passed these three at 553966eaa and vf30 failed them at 4761ef4fd. The assignment states the bytes did not move between those bases. This lane confirmed the second half of that at its own base before editing anything: sha256sum over the twelve committed fixtures at 85846c48d reproduces every digest vf30 recorded, and re-running each UNCHANGED builder at 85846c48d reproduced all four PDFs of each family byte for byte (git reported no diff on any fixtures/ path).
theBytesDidNotMoveBeforeThisLaneTouchedT.consequence: Every byte that moves in this lane is attributable to this repair and to nothing else.

howTheSourceWasRendered.why: A removed-dark-pixel count taken against an ANNOTATION-FREE render of an AcroForm source is worthless. These four Indiana forms keep much of what the court prints inside widget /AP /N appearance streams, so an annotation-free source render is missing exactly the ink whose absence from the delivered page the difference is meant to detect: both sides come up blank in the same places and the difference is zero by construction. That failure mode has already produced a published zero over 27,981 erased pixels on two other Indiana families.
howTheSourceWasRendered.renderer: poppler pdftoppm, invoked as `pdftoppm -r 300 -gray -aa yes -f <page> -l <page> <pdf> <prefix>`, directly on the pinned PDF in mounted custody. Poppler draws widget annotation appearance streams by default and no flag was passed to suppress them.
howTheSourceWasRendered.resolution: 300 dpi grayscale, 2550x3300 px on every letter page measured.
howTheSourceWasRendered.threshold: PRIMARY READING: grey <= 128 counts as a dark pixel. The same difference was also taken at grey <= 96, <= 112, <= 144 and <= 160 and the added and removed figures are identical at every cut, which is the plateau this lane reads from. The dark-pixel TOTALS move a great deal across that sweep (page 4 of the d6 source reads 352,999 / 363,235 / 371,098 / 383,453 / 403,320 at those five cuts), which is exactly why the threshold is published beside every count here.
howTheSourceWasRendered.provedNotAssumed: For each family the pinned insert was also loaded with pdf-lib, every page /Annots deleted and the catalog /AcroForm dropped, saved, and rendered with the identical command as a control. Differencing the control against the annotated render of the same page at grey <= 128 / 300 dpi gives 13,951 dark pixels on the d6 insert page that are drawn ONLY when annotations are drawn, and 12,359 in the reverse direction where widget /MK /BG backgrounds paint over page content. A blind render would have produced 0 in the first direction. The render draws widget /AP /N ink, so the zeros it produced mean something. The control copy was used only as a proof and never as a comparison baseline.
howTheSourceWasRendered.whatThisLaneDidNotDo: It dispatched no raster. No local render here is a receipt.
howTheSourceWasRendered.aKnownRendererWarning: pdftoppm emits `Syntax Error: Missing language pack for 'Adobe-Korea1' mapping` on these sources. It is emitted identically on the source render and on the packet render of the same page, so it cannot bias a directional difference; it is recorded here because it means a small number of CJK-mapped glyphs may be absent from BOTH sides of every comparison.

whyNoFlattenWasIntroduced.theInstruction: vf30 was sent to decide whether these three lost the court's printed writing rules the way their Section 1 siblings did, and found they did not: removed and added are 0 and 0 on all seven retained pages of all three families, on both fixtures, measured over the WHOLE page rather than after excluding widget rects. whatContradictsACommittedRecord.what: vf30 recorded KNOWN_PREFILLS as PASS on THIS family. This lane measured a defect of the same class vf30 failed the felony sibling for, in this family's BOUNDARY fixture, and did not repair it.
whatContradictsACommittedRecord.theMeasurement: in_conviction_d6-set's boundary fixture writes cause number '45C01-0812-FB-00000000000123456' into both captions and, three lines below, 'Offense level as it appears on the court record: Class D felony under the pre-2014 sentencing scheme, treated as a Level 6 felony conviction'. The charge-level token inside that cause number is FB. The IDENTICAL cause-number string is used by in_conviction_felony-set's boundary fixture, where the stated level is 'Class B felony under the pre-2014 sentencing scheme' - and vf30 cited that very pairing as INTERNALLY CONSISTENT, which is what makes the same string beside 'Class D felony' read as the same copied constant vf30 failed the felony canonical for.
whatContradictsACommittedRecord.theSymmetry: vf30 found 49D01-1503-F6-011234 correct in d6 canonical (Level 6) and wrong in felony canonical (Level 5). 45C01-0812-FB-... is the mirror image: correct in felony boundary (Class B) and wrong in d6 boundary (Class D). vf30 checked the canonical caption facts on this family and did not check the boundary ones.
whatContradictsACommittedRecord.whyThisLaneDidNotFixIt: The repair grant on this family names ARTIFACTS and REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING, and the assignment scopes the KNOWN_PREFILLS repair to in_conviction_felony-set alone. vf30 measured KNOWN_PREFILLS on this family as PASS. Widening a bounded repair on my own inference, on a fixture fact a verifier examined and passed, is the wrong way round: this belongs in a verifier's measurement and then in a bounded grant, not in a builder's judgement. It is reported here in full so it can be dispatched.
whatContradictsACommittedRecord.andACaveatOnMyOwnInference: The token-to-level correspondence this rests on is NOT established by any controlling record in this repository - see the felony row's causeNumberAuthority. It is an internal convention this repository already uses in five of the six Indiana fixture cause numbers. On the misd boundary the rule is genuinely ambiguous, because a Class A misdemeanor reduced from a Class D felony under I.C. 35-50-2-7 would ordinarily keep the cause number it was charged under. FB beside 'Class D felony' fails under every reading of the convention, which is why it is reported; a reviewer should still treat the convention itself as unsourced.

causeNumberAuthority.theQuestionTheAssignmentAsked: Whether the controlling record establishes a cause number for this route, in which case the value should come from it rather than be invented.
causeNumberAuthority.theAnswer: IT DOES NOT, AND THIS IS SAID RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. data/record-clearing/legal-design-intake/IN.memo.json - the controlling record for this track - carries the cause number only as a QUESTION PUT TO THE PARTICIPANT ('What is the cause number?', line 842 and again at 1203, 1552, 1911) and as something to ask the clerk about ('Ask the clerk for the balance on the cause number'). It states no cause number, and no source in this repository or in mounted custody states one for this route.
causeNumberAuthority.andNoTokenTableEitherAndThatIsStatedToo: No record in this repository establishes an Indiana charge-level-to-case-type token convention. Grepping the whole repository for the string 'F6-' returns exactly four hits and all four are this defect: the two builders' fixture constants and the two reports that echo them. The pinned insert CCA-XP-0220-7010 prints cause-number and 'Related MC cause numbers' fields but publishes no token table.
causeNumberAuthority.soOnWhatAuthorityTheTokenWasChanged: On internal consistency alone, and on nothing else. The cause number here is FIXTURE DATA, not a record fact - it exercises the caption write and it stands in for a value a real participant supplies. The obligation on fixture data is that it must not make the delivered page contradict itself, and F6 beside 'Level 5 felony' did. F5 was chosen because it is the token this repository's own five other Indiana fixture cause numbers already use for their stated level (F6 beside Level 6 in d6 canonical, FB beside Class B felony in this family's boundary, CM beside Class A misdemeanor in both misd fixtures). NO INDIANA CLERK PRACTICE IS ASSERTED as record fact by this change, no filing fee, service rule, deadline or judicial finding was invented, and a reviewer should treat the token convention itself as unsourced.
causeNumberAuthority.whatWasDeliberatelyNotDone: The offence level was not changed to match the token. The offence level is the route's defining fact - this family is the I.C. 35-38-9-4 track for felonies not covered by 35-38-9-2 or 35-38-9-3 - and moving it to fit a fixture identifier would have been the wrong repair. No new cause number was composed, and no digits beyond the two-character token were altered.

whatContradictsACommittedRecord.what: A caveat on this lane's own token reasoning, recorded against this family because this is where it is visible.
whatContradictsACommittedRecord.theMeasurement: This family's boundary fixture pairs cause number 45C01-0812-CM-00000000000123456 with 'Class A misdemeanor reduced from a Class D felony under I.C. 35-50-2-7'. Under the naive rule that a cause number's charge-level token must match the offence level the page states, CM is right. Under the equally ordinary reading that a cause number is assigned at charging and does not change when a felony is later reduced, the token would be FD. Both readings are defensible and NO RECORD IN THIS REPOSITORY SETTLES WHICH APPLIES.
whatContradictsACommittedRecord.whyItIsRecordedRatherThanActedOn: Nothing was changed here.
